title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：orange　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 orange 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1994 the cook ① peeled the orange that no guest in the canteen would have described, and he said the peeling was the whole of the day. The ② orange, meaning the fruit itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed undescribed in the book; an orange, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ orange in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ orange at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An orange, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the cook said the describing is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the orange was the whole of the matter, meaning the sweetness and not the fruit. The ⑥ orange, meaning the sweetness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; orange, he said, is either something you peel or the only word that means both a fruit and a sweetness. He said the sweetness is the part they remember.

By 1999 the ⑦ orange had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ orange of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of describing; orange, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ orange I remember is the fruit described in the menu, which closed in 2001 and is still described as the quietest in the canteen. An ⑩ orange, my mother said in 2003, is the only fruit that improves by being described; every orange, she said, is a sweetness that has agreed to look like a fruit. She said the sweetness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 橙子；橘子（指食堂里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 橙子；橘子（指那个橙子本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：peel the orange 剥这一个橙子
D. n. 橙子；橘子（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 橙子之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的橙子之事）
F. n. 橙子；橘子（指菜单里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 橙子、甜头（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 甜头（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: peeled the orange that no guest in the canteen would have described
The orange, meaning the fruit itself and not the bowl
the orange at the far table

answers.why: peel the orange 意为“剥这一个橙子”，1994 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯描述的一个橙子做了一遍。
orange 意为“橙子；橘子”，指那个橙子本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被描述。
orange 意为“橙子；橘子”，指食堂里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
orange 意为“橙子；橘子”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
orange 意为“橙子、甜头”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个甜头就是那件事的全部。
orange 意为“甜头”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个橙子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
orange 意为“橙子；橘子”，指菜单里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1999 年这一个成了菜单里的一行。
orange 意为“橙子之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的橙子之事是一处食堂和三个日子的描述。
orange 意为“橙子；橘子”，我记得的是菜单里描述过的那一个，2001 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一个。
orange 为抽象总称，母亲 2003 年说，橙子是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的橙子。
